key_insight: Homogeneous WC–Co–Cr powder produces dense, layered cermet coatings, while the spray process shifts the balance between hardness and tribological performance.
engineering_relevance: Selecting DS or HVOF lets engineers tune WC–Co–Cr coatings for wear-resistant machine parts depending on whether maximum hardness or lower friction is the priority.
method: Compared detonation spray (DS) and high-velocity oxy-fuel (HVOF) deposition of WC–Co–Cr coatings.
Characterized powder morphology and coating microstructure using SEM and EDS.
Compared phase/microstructure outcomes and tribological indicators across the two processes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an average microhardness of 1449 HV for DS coatings and a low friction coefficient (Kt = 0.143) for HVOF coatings, supporting a process-dependent tradeoff in performance.
watch_item: Results depend strongly on powder homogeneity and spraying conditions, so the reported advantages may not transfer to poorly alloyed feedstock or different process settings.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
